newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian farm produce exports up 4.94 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian farm produce exports up 4.94 pct in 1996.

text.p: Agricultural exports by Nigeria in 1996 totalled 362,233.80 tonnes, a rise of 4.94 percent from 345,169.10 tonnes the year before, according to official data.
The federal produce inspection services figures showed cocoa for the second year running topped farm produce export at 167,651.88 tonnes or 46.3 percent of the total.
Total earnings from agricultural exports in 1996 was $298.32 million compared with $263.23 million in 1995.
Cocoa accounted for $209.56 million in 1996 from $177.38 million in 1995.
The other significant farm export was palm kernel cake, which stood at 124,113.07 tonnes in 1996 from 123,999.84 tonnes in 1995.
Other exports, in small quantities, included cassava chips, rubber, gum arabic, sesame seeds, cashew nuts, shea butter and ginger.

Before Nigeria became a major oil exporter from which it derives the bulk of the average $10 billion of annual export income, the West African nation was a major producer of a variety of crops including palm oil.
A new government policy is targetting the revival of the farm sector.
